events.title: The earliest human presence
events.description: Stone tools at Monte Poggiolo and a butchered elephant at Isernia put early humans in Italy well before our own species, among the oldest such sites in Europe.

events.title: Modern humans arrive
events.description: Teeth from the Grotta del Cavallo in Apulia are among the oldest anatomically modern human remains in Europe, overlapping with the last Neanderthals.

events.title: Farming arrives from the east
events.description: Neolithic farmers cross the Adriatic into Apulia with wheat, sheep and pottery, and agriculture spreads up the peninsula over the next two thousand years.

events.title: Otzi dies in the Alps
events.description: A man is killed by an arrow high in the Otztal Alps and freezes into a glacier, to emerge in 1991 as the best-preserved prehistoric body ever found.

events.title: The Terramare of the Po valley
events.description: Bronze Age villages on raised platforms spread across the Po plain, farming, casting bronze and trading amber down from the Baltic.

events.title: The Villanovan culture
events.description: Iron-working cremation communities appear in Tuscany and Emilia. They are the direct ancestors of the Etruscans.

events.title: Etruscan civilisation emerges
events.description: City-states rise across Etruria with metalworking, monumental tombs, a written alphabet and a language still not fully understood.

events.title: Greeks settle at Pithecusae and Cumae
events.description: Euboean colonists found the first Greek settlements in the west, beginning the string of cities the Romans later call Magna Graecia.

events.title: The founding of Rome
events.description: Roman tradition dates the founding of the city to 753 BCE. Archaeology finds a village on the Palatine at about the right time, but not the wolf.

events.title: Syracuse founded
events.description: Corinthian settlers found Syracuse in Sicily. It grows into one of the largest cities in the Greek world and beats Athens in war.

events.title: Etruscan kings rule Rome
events.description: Tarquinius Priscus becomes king. Under the Etruscan monarchy Rome gets its drainage, its forum, its temples and its first city walls.

events.title: The Cloaca Maxima drains the forum
events.description: A great sewer is cut to drain the marsh between the hills, turning the valley into the Forum Romanum. Parts of it still carry water.

events.title: The Republic founded
events.description: The last king is expelled and Rome becomes a republic governed by two annually elected consuls and a senate - a constitution that lasts nearly five centuries.

events.title: The tribunes of the plebs
events.description: The plebeians secede from the city until they are granted their own magistrates with the power to veto. Class conflict becomes a constitutional mechanism.

events.title: The Twelve Tables
events.description: Roman law is written down and displayed publicly for the first time, which stops the patrician priests being the only people who know what it says.

events.title: Veii destroyed
events.description: After a ten-year siege Rome takes the nearest Etruscan city and doubles its territory. The method - siege, annexation, absorption - becomes the pattern.

events.title: The Gauls sack Rome
events.description: A Gallic army destroys a Roman force at the Allia and burns the city. The trauma shapes Roman policy towards the north for three hundred years.

events.title: The Samnite Wars
events.description: Three long wars against the mountain confederation of Samnium give Rome control of central and southern Italy, and give the legion its flexible manipular formation.

events.title: The Appian Way and the first aqueduct
events.description: Appius Claudius builds a paved military road south to Capua and an aqueduct into the city in the same censorship. Roads and water become instruments of state.

events.title: Pyrrhus invades
events.description: The king of Epirus wins two battles against Rome at ruinous cost and then withdraws, leaving the phrase Pyrrhic victory and Rome master of the whole peninsula.

events.title: The First Punic War begins
events.description: A dispute over Messina turns into a twenty-three-year naval war with Carthage. Rome has no fleet at the start and wins the war at sea.

events.title: Sicily becomes the first province
events.description: Carthage sues for peace and cedes Sicily. Rome now governs territory outside Italy, and the machinery of empire begins.

events.title: Hannibal crosses the Alps
events.description: Hannibal takes an army and elephants over the Alps into Italy, and spends the next fifteen years undefeated on Roman soil.

events.title: Cannae
events.description: Hannibal encircles and destroys the largest army Rome ever put in the field. Somewhere between fifty and seventy thousand Romans die in a day.

events.title: Zama ends the war
events.description: Scipio defeats Hannibal in Africa. Carthage is stripped of its empire and Rome is left without a rival in the western Mediterranean.

events.title: Macedon defeated at Pydna
events.description: The Roman victory at Pydna ends Macedonian independence and effectively makes Rome the arbiter of the Greek east.

events.title: Carthage and Corinth destroyed
events.description: Both cities are razed in the same year. Roman hegemony over the Mediterranean is now a fact, and Greek art, slaves and ideas flood into Italy.

events.title: Tiberius Gracchus killed
events.description: A tribune pushing land redistribution is beaten to death by senators. Political violence enters Roman public life and never leaves.

events.title: The Marian reforms
events.description: Marius opens the legions to the landless poor and reorganises them around the cohort. Soldiers now depend on their general rather than their farm.

events.title: The Social War
events.description: Rome's Italian allies revolt over citizenship and are defeated, then granted exactly what they had demanded. Italy south of the Po becomes Roman.

events.title: Sulla's dictatorship
events.description: Sulla marches on Rome, proscribes his enemies and rewrites the constitution. He then resigns, having proved that the army can decide who governs.

events.title: The revolt of Spartacus
events.description: A gladiator leads the largest slave rising in Roman history, beats several Roman armies and is finally crushed by Crassus, who crucifies six thousand survivors.

events.title: The First Triumvirate
events.description: Caesar, Pompey and Crassus divide the state between them privately. The senate becomes a spectator.

events.title: Caesar crosses the Rubicon
events.description: Caesar brings a legion across the river into Italy, which is treason by definition. The civil war he starts ends the Republic in practice.

events.title: Caesar assassinated
events.description: Sixty senators stab Caesar in the Theatre of Pompey to save the Republic, and destroy what was left of it in the process.

events.title: Actium
events.description: Octavian's fleet defeats Antony and Cleopatra off western Greece. One man is left in control of the Roman world.

events.title: Augustus and the principate
events.description: Octavian hands his powers back to the senate and is given them again as Augustus. The Republic is preserved in form and replaced in substance.

events.title: The Aeneid published
events.description: Virgil dies leaving the Aeneid unfinished. It gives Rome a founding myth of Trojan descent and becomes the central text of Latin literature.

events.title: The Great Fire of Rome
events.description: Fire burns for six days and destroys much of the city. Nero rebuilds on a new plan and blames the Christians, beginning the first persecution.

events.title: Vesuvius buries Pompeii
events.description: Vesuvius erupts and buries Pompeii, Herculaneum and Stabiae under ash and surge deposits, preserving three Roman towns in the act of dying.

events.title: The Colosseum opens
events.description: The Flavian Amphitheatre is inaugurated with a hundred days of games. It seats fifty thousand and remains the largest amphitheatre ever built.

events.title: The empire at its greatest extent
events.description: Trajan dies having annexed Dacia and Mesopotamia. The empire reaches from the Solway to the Persian Gulf, and never gets bigger.

events.title: The Pantheon rebuilt
events.description: Hadrian rebuilds the Pantheon with an unreinforced concrete dome forty-three metres across - still the largest of its kind in the world.

events.title: Marcus Aurelius
events.description: The last of the five good emperors rules through plague and German invasion, writing the Meditations in camp. His death ends the long peace.

events.title: The Antonine Plague
events.description: An epidemic, probably smallpox, kills perhaps a tenth of the empire's population and hollows out the army at the moment it is most needed.

events.title: Citizenship for every free man
events.description: Caracalla extends Roman citizenship to all free inhabitants of the empire. It broadens the tax base and dissolves the distinction Rome was built on.

events.title: The crisis of the third century
events.description: Fifty years of civil war, invasion, plague and currency collapse nearly end the empire. More than twenty men claim the throne.

events.title: Diocletian reorganises the empire
events.description: Diocletian splits the administration, doubles the number of provinces and fixes the currency. The empire survives, but as something much more bureaucratic.

events.title: The Edict of Milan
events.description: Constantine and Licinius grant toleration to Christians. Within a lifetime the persecuted church becomes the imperial one.

events.title: The capital moves east
events.description: Constantine dedicates Constantinople. Rome remains the symbolic centre and stops being where anything is decided.

events.title: Christianity becomes the state religion
events.description: Theodosius makes Nicene Christianity the official religion of the empire and closes the temples. The pagan Roman state is over.

events.title: Ravenna becomes the western capital
events.description: The western court moves to Ravenna for its marshes and its harbour. For the next three centuries it is the political centre of Italy.

events.title: Alaric sacks Rome
events.description: A Visigothic army enters Rome and plunders it for three days. The city has not fallen to a foreign enemy in eight hundred years, and the shock is felt everywhere.

events.title: Attila turned back
events.description: Attila invades northern Italy, destroys Aquileia and then withdraws after meeting Pope Leo I. Refugees from Aquileia are later credited with founding Venice.

events.title: The Vandals sack Rome
events.description: Genseric's Vandals take Rome from the sea and strip it methodically over fourteen days, including the roof of the Temple of Jupiter.

events.title: The last western emperor deposed
events.description: Odoacer deposes Romulus Augustulus and sends the imperial regalia to Constantinople, declining to appoint a successor. It is the conventional end of the western empire.

events.title: Theodoric's Ostrogothic kingdom
events.description: Theodoric rules Italy from Ravenna with Roman law and a Gothic army, keeps the senate and builds churches. It is the last time Italy is prosperous for centuries.

events.title: Boethius writes in prison
events.description: Awaiting execution for treason, Boethius writes the Consolation of Philosophy, the book that carries classical thought into the Middle Ages.

events.title: Benedict founds Monte Cassino
events.description: Benedict of Nursia establishes a monastery and writes a rule for it. Western monasticism, and much of the survival of literacy, follows from it.

events.title: The Gothic War devastates Italy
events.description: Justinian reconquers Italy for the eastern empire in twenty years of war that ruin the peninsula, depopulate Rome and destroy the senatorial order.

events.title: The Lombards invade
events.description: A Germanic confederation crosses the Alps and takes most of the interior. Italy splits into Lombard duchies and Byzantine coastal strips - a division that lasts.

events.title: Gregory the Great elected
events.description: With no functioning imperial government in Rome, Pope Gregory feeds the city, negotiates with the Lombards and sends missionaries to England. The papacy becomes a temporal power.

events.title: The Lombards take Ravenna
events.description: The fall of the Byzantine exarchate leaves the pope without an imperial protector, so he looks north for one.

events.title: The Donation of Pepin
events.description: Pepin the Short takes the former exarchate from the Lombards and grants it to the papacy, creating the Papal States. They last until 1870.

events.title: Charlemagne conquers the Lombards
events.description: Charlemagne takes Pavia and the Lombard crown. Northern Italy is absorbed into the Frankish realm and reoriented towards Europe.

events.title: Charlemagne crowned emperor in Rome
events.description: Leo III crowns Charlemagne Emperor of the Romans in St Peter's. The western empire is revived as a partnership between Frankish arms and papal legitimacy.

events.title: The Arab conquest of Sicily begins
events.description: Aghlabid forces land at Mazara. Over the next seventy-five years Sicily becomes Muslim, and for two centuries Palermo is one of the great cities of the Mediterranean.

events.title: Otto I crowned in Rome
events.description: The German king is crowned emperor, tying Italy to the Holy Roman Empire and starting nine centuries of German intervention in Italian politics.

events.title: The maritime republics rise
events.description: Venice, Genoa, Pisa and Amalfi build fleets and trading networks across the Mediterranean, growing rich on the carrying trade and effectively independent.

events.title: Pisa begins its cathedral
events.description: Financed by plunder from a raid on Palermo, Pisa starts the cathedral complex that eventually includes the leaning campanile.

events.title: The Normans take Bari
events.description: Robert Guiscard captures the last Byzantine stronghold in Italy. Within twenty years the Normans hold the whole south and Sicily.

events.title: Canossa
events.description: Emperor Henry IV waits three days in the snow for absolution from Gregory VII. The Investiture Controversy sets pope against emperor and gives the Italian cities room to grow.

events.title: The University of Bologna
events.description: Law teaching at Bologna organises itself into a studium. It is generally reckoned the oldest university in continuous operation in the world.

events.title: The Kingdom of Sicily founded
events.description: Roger II is crowned at Palermo over a state that fuses Norman, Arab, Greek and Latin administration, and is for a while the best-run kingdom in Europe.

events.title: Legnano
events.description: The Lombard League defeats Frederick Barbarossa. The northern communes win the right to govern themselves, and Italy's political fragmentation is locked in.

events.title: Venice diverts the Fourth Crusade
events.description: Venice steers the crusade onto Constantinople, sacks it, and takes three-eighths of the Byzantine empire including Crete. It becomes a maritime empire.

events.title: Frederick II and the Sicilian court
events.description: Frederick II rules Sicily and the empire from Palermo, legislating, hunting with falcons, arguing with popes and hosting the first school of Italian poetry.

events.title: Charles of Anjou takes the south
events.description: Angevin French rule replaces the Hohenstaufen in Naples and Sicily, and the papacy has a new secular patron in the peninsula.

events.title: The Sicilian Vespers
events.description: A rising in Palermo against the French brings in the Aragonese and splits the kingdom. Sicily and Naples go separate ways for a century and a half.

events.title: Meloria
events.description: Genoa destroys the Pisan fleet at Meloria and takes thousands of prisoners. Pisa never recovers as a naval power.

events.title: Florence begins its cathedral
events.description: The commune commissions a cathedral so large that nobody yet knows how to roof it. The problem waits a hundred and twenty years for Brunelleschi.

events.title: The first Jubilee
events.description: Boniface VIII proclaims a holy year and Rome fills with pilgrims. It is the high-water mark of papal claims, and Dante is in the city to see it.

events.title: The papacy moves to Avignon
events.description: Clement V settles the curia at Avignon under French protection. For sixty-eight years there is no pope in Rome, and the city decays.

events.title: Dante finishes the Divine Comedy
events.description: Dante completes the Comedy in exile at Ravenna, in Tuscan, and in doing so makes a dialect into a literary language.

events.title: The Black Death lands at Messina
events.description: Plague arrives on Genoese galleys from the Black Sea and spreads through Italy within months, killing perhaps half the population of Florence.

events.title: The Ciompi revolt
events.description: Florentine wool workers seize the government and hold it for six weeks. It is one of the first urban working-class risings in European history.

events.title: The baptistery doors competition
events.description: Florence holds a competition for a set of bronze doors. Ghiberti beats Brunelleschi, and the episode is traditionally taken as the start of the Renaissance.

events.title: Brunelleschi begins the dome
events.description: Brunelleschi starts the cathedral dome without centering, using a double shell and a herringbone brick pattern. It is still the largest masonry dome ever built.

events.title: Cosimo de' Medici takes control of Florence
events.description: A banker governs the republic without holding office, through credit, patronage and marriage. The family runs Florence for most of the next three centuries.

events.title: The Peace of Lodi
events.description: Milan, Venice, Florence, Naples and the papacy agree a balance of power. Forty years of relative peace let the Renaissance become expensive.

events.title: Lorenzo the Magnificent
events.description: Lorenzo de' Medici inherits Florence at twenty and turns patronage into statecraft, keeping Botticelli, Michelangelo and half the humanists of Italy in work.

events.title: The French invade
events.description: Charles VIII marches to Naples almost unopposed, exposing how weak the Italian states are. Italy becomes the battlefield of Europe for sixty years.

events.title: Savonarola burned
events.description: The friar who had ruled Florence as a republic of virtue is hanged and burned in the Piazza della Signoria, where he had burned other people's books.

events.title: Leonardo begins the Mona Lisa
events.description: Leonardo starts the portrait in Florence and is still working on it years later in France. He leaves behind notebooks a century ahead of anyone.

events.title: The Sistine Chapel ceiling
events.description: Michelangelo paints the vault for Julius II in four years, largely alone and against his own preference for sculpture.

events.title: Machiavelli writes The Prince
events.description: Out of office and under suspicion, Machiavelli writes a short book about how power actually works rather than how it ought to. It is not published until after his death.

events.title: The Sack of Rome
events.description: Unpaid imperial troops storm Rome and loot it for weeks. The Renaissance papacy is humiliated and the artists scatter across Europe.

events.title: Florence falls and the republic ends
events.description: After an eleven-month siege the Medici return as hereditary dukes under imperial protection. The last major Italian republic apart from Venice is finished.

events.title: The Council of Trent
events.description: The church meets at Trento for eighteen years to answer the Reformation. Catholic doctrine is fixed, seminaries are founded and the Index is drawn up.

events.title: Spain takes control
events.description: The Peace of Cateau-Cambresis leaves Spain holding Milan, Naples, Sicily and Sardinia. Most of Italy is governed from Madrid for the next century and a half.

events.title: Lepanto
events.description: A Christian fleet led by Venice and Spain destroys the Ottoman navy off Greece. It is the last great galley battle and it does not change much.

events.title: Giordano Bruno burned
events.description: The Inquisition burns Bruno in the Campo de' Fiori for heresy, including his belief in an infinite universe of other worlds.

events.title: Galileo publishes the telescopic discoveries
events.description: Galileo reports mountains on the moon and four moons around Jupiter. The heavens turn out to be made of the same stuff as everything else.

events.title: Galileo condemned
events.description: Forced to abjure heliocentrism, Galileo is sentenced to house arrest for life. Italian science, which had led Europe, largely stops leading it.

events.title: Masaniello's revolt in Naples
events.description: A fisherman leads a rising against Spanish taxation and briefly controls the second largest city in Europe.

events.title: Plague halves Naples
events.description: An epidemic kills something like half the population of Naples in six months, and the southern economy does not recover for generations.

events.title: Austria replaces Spain
events.description: The Treaty of Utrecht transfers Milan, Naples and Sardinia to the Austrian Habsburgs. The occupier changes; the arrangement does not.

events.title: The Medici line ends
events.description: The last Medici Grand Duke dies and Tuscany passes to Lorraine. His sister leaves the family's entire art collection to the city on condition it never leaves.

events.title: Pompeii excavated
events.description: Systematic digging begins at Pompeii. The finds shape European taste for a century and effectively invent classical archaeology.

events.title: Beccaria on crime and punishment
events.description: Beccaria argues against torture and the death penalty in a short book that is read across Europe and changes law in a dozen countries.

events.title: Tuscany abolishes the death penalty
events.description: Grand Duke Peter Leopold abolishes capital punishment and torture in Tuscany, the first state anywhere to do so.

events.title: Napoleon invades Italy
events.description: A twenty-six-year-old general takes northern Italy in a year, abolishes ancient states and carries off their art. Nothing goes back to how it was.

events.title: The Republic of Venice extinguished
events.description: Napoleon ends eleven hundred years of Venetian independence with a treaty and hands the city to Austria. The last doge simply goes home.

events.title: Napoleon crowned King of Italy
events.description: Napoleon takes the iron crown at Milan. French administration, the Napoleonic code and conscription give Italians their first taste of a single state.

events.title: The Congress of Vienna restores the old order
events.description: Italy is put back together as seven states under Austrian supervision, described by Metternich as a geographical expression. The restoration creates the movement against it.

events.title: The Carbonari risings
events.description: Secret societies force constitutions out of Naples and Piedmont, and Austrian troops take them back within months.

events.title: Mazzini founds Young Italy
events.description: In exile in Marseille, Mazzini founds a movement for a unified Italian republic built on insurrection and national education rather than diplomacy.

events.title: Verdi and the Risorgimento
events.description: Nabucco opens at La Scala and the chorus of exiled Hebrews becomes an unofficial anthem. Opera turns into a way of saying things the censors forbid.

events.title: The year of revolutions
events.description: Risings in Palermo, Milan and Venice force constitutions across Italy and start a war with Austria. Only the Piedmontese constitution survives the reaction.

events.title: The Roman Republic and its fall
events.description: Mazzini and Garibaldi govern Rome for five months after the pope flees. French troops restore him, and Garibaldi walks out through the Apennines.

events.title: Cavour becomes prime minister of Piedmont
events.description: Cavour modernises Piedmont's economy and then goes looking for a great-power ally, on the view that Italy cannot be unified without one.

events.title: The Second War of Independence
events.description: With French help Piedmont beats Austria at Magenta and Solferino and takes Lombardy. Nice and Savoy are the price.

events.title: The Expedition of the Thousand
events.description: Garibaldi lands in Sicily with about a thousand volunteers and takes the whole Kingdom of the Two Sicilies in five months, then hands it to the king.

events.title: The Kingdom of Italy proclaimed
events.description: Victor Emmanuel II is declared King of Italy. Rome and Venetia are still outside it, and only about two per cent of the population can vote.

events.title: The southern insurgency
events.description: Resistance in the south is put down by more soldiers than fought the whole war of unification. It is called banditry at the time and civil war since.

events.title: Venetia joins Italy
events.description: Italy gains Venetia from the Prussian defeat of Austria, having lost its own battles at Custoza and Lissa.

events.title: Rome taken
events.description: With French troops withdrawn for their own war, Italian forces breach the Aurelian wall at Porta Pia. The Papal States end and unification is complete.

events.title: Rome becomes the capital
events.description: The government moves to Rome and the pope declares himself a prisoner in the Vatican, refusing to recognise the Italian state for fifty-eight years.

events.title: The great emigration
events.description: Poverty in the south sends millions abroad. Something like fourteen million people leave Italy in forty years, the largest emigration from any country in the period.

events.title: The Triple Alliance
events.description: Italy allies with Germany and Austria-Hungary, its recent enemy, mainly out of irritation at France taking Tunisia.

events.title: Defeat at Adwa
events.description: An Ethiopian army destroys an Italian force at Adwa. It is the first decisive African victory over a European colonial power and it ends the government.

events.title: King Umberto assassinated
events.description: An anarchist shoots Umberto I at Monza in revenge for the suppression of the 1898 bread riots.

events.title: The invasion of Libya
events.description: Italy takes Libya from the Ottomans, using aircraft in war for the first time anywhere, and finds the occupation far harder than the conquest.

events.title: Italy enters the war against Austria
events.description: Italy abandons the Triple Alliance for secret promises of Austrian territory and attacks along the Isonzo. Eleven battles are fought on the same river.

events.title: Caporetto
events.description: An Austro-German attack breaks the Italian line and drives the army back seventy miles. Some 300,000 men are taken prisoner and the word becomes a synonym for rout.

events.title: Victory at Vittorio Veneto
events.description: Italy breaks the Austrian army and the empire dissolves. Around 650,000 Italian soldiers have died.

events.title: The mutilated victory
events.description: Italy gets less at Versailles than it was promised, D'Annunzio seizes Fiume with irregulars, and the sense of a stolen war feeds what comes next.

events.title: The squads and the biennio rosso
events.description: Factory occupations and land seizures are met by Fascist squads burning union halls, often with the connivance of police and landowners.

events.title: The March on Rome
events.description: Mussolini's Blackshirts converge on the capital and the king appoints him prime minister rather than order the army to stop them.

events.title: Matteotti murdered
events.description: The socialist deputy who had catalogued Fascist electoral violence is abducted and killed. Mussolini uses the crisis to abolish what remains of parliament.

events.title: The Lateran Treaty
events.description: Mussolini settles the Roman question, creating the Vatican City State and buying the church's acquiescence in the regime.

events.title: The invasion of Ethiopia
events.description: Italy invades Ethiopia using poison gas and aerial bombing, is condemned by the League of Nations, and is pushed towards Germany by the sanctions.

events.title: The racial laws
events.description: Anti-Jewish legislation strips Italian Jews of jobs, schooling and civil rights, with no German pressure to do it.

events.title: Italy enters the Second World War
events.description: Mussolini declares war on France and Britain expecting a short one, and commits an unprepared country to campaigns in Greece, Africa and Russia that all go badly.

events.title: The Allies land in Sicily
events.description: Operation Husky puts Allied armies on Italian soil. Within two weeks the Fascist Grand Council votes Mussolini out and the king has him arrested.

events.title: The armistice and the German occupation
events.description: Italy surrenders to the Allies, the government flees south and Germany occupies the north. The country splits in two and the war is fought up its length.

events.title: Monte Cassino and the Gothic Line
events.description: Four battles and four months destroy the abbey at Monte Cassino. The Allies take Rome in June and are still fighting in the Apennines the following spring.

events.title: The Resistance and the civil war
events.description: Partisan bands fight the Germans and the Salo republic, and are answered with reprisals like the Ardeatine caves and Marzabotto. The Resistance becomes the founding myth of the republic.

events.title: Mussolini executed
events.description: Partisans catch Mussolini heading for Switzerland and shoot him. The bodies are hung up in the Piazzale Loreto in Milan.

events.title: Italy votes to become a republic
events.description: In the first election with universal suffrage, including women, Italians abolish the monarchy 54 to 46 and elect a constituent assembly. The Savoys go into exile.

events.title: The Constitution comes into force
events.description: A constitution written jointly by Catholics, communists and liberals takes effect. In April, with heavy American involvement, the Christian Democrats win the election.

events.title: Founding the European project
events.description: Italy is one of the six founders of the European Coal and Steel Community, using integration to anchor a young democracy to the west.

events.title: The Treaty of Rome signed
events.description: The European Economic Community is founded on the Capitoline Hill. It is the treaty from which the European Union grows.

events.title: The economic miracle
events.description: Italy grows at around six per cent a year, moves millions from the south to the northern factories and turns a largely rural country into an industrial one in fifteen years.

events.title: The Rome Olympics
events.description: The Games are held among the ruins, with the marathon finishing at the Arch of Constantine. Italy presents itself as modern and reconstructed.

events.title: The Vajont dam disaster
events.description: A landslide into a reservoir sends a wave over the dam and kills about 1,900 people. The engineering risk had been known and ignored.

events.title: The student movement
events.description: Universities are occupied across the country and the protest feeds into a wave of factory militancy that peaks in the hot autumn of 1969.

events.title: Piazza Fontana and the Years of Lead
events.description: A bomb in a Milan bank kills seventeen and opens two decades of political violence from both extremes, with parts of the state implicated in the strategy of tension.

events.title: Divorce legalised
events.description: Parliament legalises divorce, and a 1974 referendum to repeal it is defeated. Abortion follows in 1978. Italian social law shifts faster than its politics.

events.title: Aldo Moro murdered
events.description: The Red Brigades kidnap the Christian Democrat leader, hold him for fifty-five days while the state refuses to negotiate, and leave his body in a car in central Rome.

events.title: The Bologna station bombing
events.description: A neo-fascist bomb kills 85 people at Bologna station, the deadliest attack of the Years of Lead. A few months later an earthquake in Irpinia kills nearly 2,500.

events.title: The Maxi Trial
events.description: Falcone and Borsellino put 475 mafiosi on trial in a fortified courtroom in Palermo and convict 342, on evidence that the organisation exists at all.

events.title: Falcone and Borsellino killed
events.description: The Mafia kills both magistrates within two months, with half a tonne of explosive at Capaci and a car bomb in Palermo. Public revulsion produces the first serious state offensive against it.

events.title: Tangentopoli
events.description: The Clean Hands investigations expose systematic party financing through kickbacks and destroy the Christian Democrats and the Socialists, the two parties that had governed for fifty years.

events.title: Berlusconi enters politics
events.description: A media proprietor founds a party and wins the election three months later. He dominates Italian politics for the next twenty years.

events.title: Italy adopts the euro
events.description: Italy joins the single currency at its launch after a sharp fiscal effort, giving up the devaluations its industry had relied on.

events.title: The debt crisis and the technocrats
events.description: With borrowing costs at record highs Berlusconi resigns and Mario Monti forms a government of technocrats. Italian debt politics becomes European politics.

events.title: The constitutional referendum fails
events.description: Voters reject Renzi's reform of the senate, he resigns, and the anti-establishment parties are set up to win the next election.

events.title: The first Western Covid epicentre
events.description: Outbreaks in Lombardy make Italy the first Western country overwhelmed by Covid-19 and the first to impose a national lockdown. Around 190,000 die.

events.title: Giorgia Meloni becomes prime minister
events.description: Italy's first woman prime minister leads a party descended from the post-war neo-fascist tradition, and governs in continuity with Brussels on the things that cost money.
